revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Overtime Hours Limit
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Chen's team can use at most 40 hours of overtime this week to close the case. So far the team has logged 26 hours. Write an inequality for the additional overtime hours t the team can still use, solve it, and graph the solution set on a number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The inequality is 26 + t ≤ 40. Subtracting 26 from both sides: t ≤ 40 − 26 = 14. Since ≤ includes the boundary, graph a closed circle at 14 and shade left (toward smaller values), meaning the team can use 14 or fewer additional overtime hours this week.

rows.wordProblem: A detective splits 42 clues equally among 6 case boards. How many clues per board?
rows.reasonable: Yes — 7 clues per board makes sense.

rows.wordProblem: A witness says the suspect carried fewer than 10 items. If the suspect already had 3, how many more could they carry?
rows.reasonable: Yes — up to 6 more items is reasonable.

rows.wordProblem: The evidence room needs at least 50 storage bins. They already have 28. How many more do they need?

hints: If the problem uses 'is,' 'equals,' or 'gives exactly,' use an equation (=). If it uses 'at least,' 'at most,' 'more than,' or 'fewer than,' use an inequality.

optional.explanation: 'At least 12' includes 12 and any number above it, so g ≥ 12.
choiceFeedback: The mean is pulled higher by 58—does that show a typical game?

Resta 6 en los dos lados para que la x quede sola y luego calcula 14 − 6.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 8.4) Which inequality represents: 'The temperature is less than 40 degrees'?
approaching.explanation: 'Less than' means <, so the inequality is t < 40.
choiceFeedback: The median ignores how far apart the values are. Check whether this data has any outlier that would make leaving values out worthwhile.
Five values is plenty for a measure of center. A small set is only a problem when it contains extreme values.
Both measures actually work reasonably well here, since the scores are clustered close together. Decide which one uses the data most fully when there are no outliers.
Not quite. 'Less than' means <, so the inequality is t < 40.
The ≤ symbol lets the temperature be exactly 40. 'Less than 40' leaves 40 out.
An equals sign pins the temperature to a single value, but this situation describes a whole range of temperatures.
hints: Look at the scores: 8.5 up to 8.9 — all five are bunched tightly together with no unusual value.
Rule of thumb: with no outliers and balanced data, one measure uses every value fairly. With outliers, the middle value is safer. Which case is this?
First step: check for an outlier — is any score far from the others? All five sit within 0.4 points, so apply the no-outlier rule.

explanationEs: El paso de la frase clave interpretó "no más de" como mayor que, pero esa frase pone un tope al grupo: el número de estudiantes nunca puede pasar de 25. Significa "a lo más", así que el modelo es s ≤ 25, que permite 25 y todos los conteos menores.
correctWorkEs: 'No más de' significa menor o igual que (≤), no mayor que. La desigualdad correcta es s ≤ 25.

correctWorkEs.title: (Lesson 8.5) Find the Graphing Error

workedExample.label: Graph
workedExample.workEs: Círculo cerrado en 6, sombreado a la derecha

correctWorkEs.correctWork: x > 6 uses a strict inequality (no 'equal to'), so the circle should be OPEN, not closed. Open circle at 6, shaded right.
hints: Q1 is not just a value in the lower half — it is the MEDIAN of the lower half.
Lower half: 3, 7, 9. The median of these three values is 7, not 9.
correctWorkEs.titleEs: Encuentra el error del diagrama de caja
correctWorkEs.explanation: The quartile step used 9, the last number in the lower half, instead of the middle of that half. The lower half is 3, 7, 9, so its median — and therefore Q1 — is 7. Q3 = 18 was already right, since 18 sits in the middle of 15, 18, 21.
correctWorkEs.explanationEs: El paso de los cuartiles usó 9, el último número de la mitad inferior, en vez del valor del medio de esa mitad. La mitad inferior es 3, 7, 9, así que su mediana —y por lo tanto Q1— es 7. Q3 = 18 ya estaba bien, porque 18 queda en el medio de 15, 18, 21.
Q1 is not just a value in the lower half — it is the MEDIAN of the lower half.
Lower half: 3, 7, 9. The median of these three values is 7, not 9.

correctWorkEs: Look at the inequality symbol carefully. Is it > or ≥?
> means strictly greater than — 6 is NOT included, so the circle must be open.
titleEs: Encuentra el error de la gráfica
explanation: The shading right matches x > 6, but the circle type step used a closed circle. Since > is strict, 6 > 6 is false and 6 is not a solution, so the graph needs an open circle at 6 shaded right.
explanationEs: El sombreado a la derecha coincide con x > 6, pero el paso del tipo de círculo usó un círculo cerrado. Como > es estricto, 6 > 6 es falso y el 6 no es solución, así que la gráfica necesita un círculo abierto en 6 sombreado a la derecha.
correctWorkEs: x > 6 usa una desigualdad estricta (sin 'igual a'), así que el círculo debe ser ABIERTO, no cerrado. Círculo abierto en 6, sombreado a la derecha.

correctWorkEs.title: (Lesson 8.6) Find the Solving Error

workedExample.label: Graph
workedExample.workEs: Círculo cerrado en 7, sombrea a la derecha

correctWorkEs.correctWork: The inverse of subtracting 8 is ADDING 8, not subtracting. Add 8 to both sides: x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23. Graph: closed circle at 23, shade right.
hints: Symmetric means the left side mirrors the right side. Does 1, 2, 3, 4, 2 mirror evenly?
The peak (4) is in the 80–89 range, which is toward the right. That means most data is on the high end.
correctWorkEs.explanation: The frequency table is right; the Conclusion step is what fails. Symmetric means the left half mirrors the right half, but 1, 2, 3, 4, 2 climbs steadily and peaks at 80–89 near the right end, so the data is skewed left with most scores on the high side.
correctWorkEs.explanationEs: La tabla de frecuencias está bien; lo que falla es el paso de la Conclusión. Simétrico significa que la mitad izquierda refleja la derecha, pero 1, 2, 3, 4, 2 sube de manera constante y llega a su punto máximo en 80–89, cerca del extremo derecho, así que los datos están sesgados a la izquierda con la mayoría de las calificaciones en el lado alto.
Symmetric means the left side mirrors the right side. Does 1, 2, 3, 4, 2 mirror evenly?
The peak (4) is in the 80–89 range, which is toward the right. That means most data is on the high end.

correctWorkEs: The equation has − 8. What is the inverse of subtracting 8?
To undo − 8, you add 8 to both sides: x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23.
explanation: The inequality shows − 8, and the inverse of subtracting is adding. Adding 8 to both sides gives x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23, not 7. The graph is a closed circle at 23 shaded to the right, since ≥ includes the boundary value.
explanationEs: La desigualdad muestra − 8, y lo inverso de restar es sumar. Al sumar 8 en ambos lados: x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23, no 7. La gráfica lleva un círculo cerrado en 23 sombreado hacia la derecha, porque ≥ incluye el valor límite.
correctWorkEs: La inversa de restar 8 es SUMAR 8, no restar. Suma 8 a ambos lados: x ≥ 15 + 8 = 23. Gráfica: círculo cerrado en 23, sombrea a la derecha.

correctWorkEs.title: (Lesson 8.7) Find the Problem-Solving Error

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: A parking lot holds at most 200 cars. There are 134 already. How many more can park?
workedExample.workEs: Un estacionamiento admite como máximo 200 autos. Ya hay 134. ¿Cuántos más pueden estacionarse?

correctWorkEs.correctWork: 'At most' means less than or equal to, so the model should be an inequality: 134 + c ≤ 200. Solving: c ≤ 66. Up to 66 more cars can park, not exactly 66.
hints: The direction of the skew is the direction of the TAIL, not the peak. Where is the long tail?
The peak is on the left (10–11 seconds) and the tail stretches right to 14.8. That means skewed RIGHT.
correctWorkEs.explanation: The shape was named from the tall bar instead of the tail. The histogram clusters at 10–11 seconds, shows empty intervals at 12 and 13, and then has one lone value at 14.8, so the stretched-out tail points right — skewed right. And because the data is skewed, the median describes a typical sprint time better than the mean, which the 14.8 pulls upward.
correctWorkEs.explanationEs: La forma se nombró por la barra alta en lugar de por la cola. El histograma se agrupa entre 10 y 11 segundos, muestra intervalos vacíos en 12 y 13, y luego tiene un solo valor en 14.8, así que la cola alargada apunta a la derecha: sesgada a la derecha. Y como los datos están sesgados, la mediana describe mejor un tiempo típico que la media, a la que el 14.8 jala hacia arriba.
The direction of the skew is the direction of the TAIL, not the peak. Where is the long tail?
The peak is on the left (10–11 seconds) and the tail stretches right to 14.8. That means skewed RIGHT.

correctWorkEs: The problem says 'at most 200.' Does that mean exactly 200 or up to 200?
'At most' requires ≤, not =. The correct model is 134 + c ≤ 200, so c ≤ 66.
titleEs: Encuentra el error al resolver el problema
explanation: The arithmetic is fine, but the model is too strict. 'At most 200 cars' means the lot can hold 200 or fewer, which is ≤, not =. The model should be 134 + c ≤ 200, giving c ≤ 66 — up to 66 more cars can park, not exactly 66.
explanationEs: Las cuentas están bien, pero el modelo es demasiado estricto. 'At most 200 cars' significa que el estacionamiento puede tener 200 o menos, y eso es ≤, no =. El modelo debe ser 134 + c ≤ 200, lo que da c ≤ 66: pueden estacionarse hasta 66 autos más, no exactamente 66.
correctWorkEs: 'Como máximo' significa menor o igual que, así que el modelo debe ser una desigualdad: 134 + c ≤ 200. Al resolver: c ≤ 66. Hasta 66 autos más pueden estacionarse, no exactamente 66.

commonMistake: A common mistake in Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving is matching the wrong model to a key phrase. For 'the getaway car held no more than 6 bags,' students often write the equation b = 6 instead of the inequality b ≤ 6, because they see one number and assume it must be exact. The same mistake happens in reverse: for 'the reward split equally among 5 people gave each $40,' students sometimes write the inequality 5p ≥ 40 instead of the equation 5p = 40, because 'split equally' sounds like it could mean a range. Before you submit, ask: does this phrase give one exact value (equation, =) or a limit/range (inequality, <, >, ≤, ≥)?

diagram.title: Detective's Budget Limit
diagram.caption: She has spent $320 of her $500 cap (closed dot = allowed), so the gap up to $500 shows r ≤ 180 — at most $180 more.

connect.scenario: A detective has a $500 budget for equipment. She has already spent $320. The inequality 320 + r ≤ 500 represents the remaining amount r she can spend. She also needs exactly 4 flashlights at $15 each, represented by the equation 4f = 60.
connect.promptQuestion: How much more can the detective spend? How much does each flashlight cost? When do you use an equation versus an inequality?
connect.prompt: The detective can spend at most $__ more because r ≤ 500 − ___ = ___. Each flashlight costs $__ because f = 60 ÷ ___ = ___.

check.explanation: Subtract 320 from both sides: r ≤ 500 − 320 = 180. She can spend at most $180 more.
Divide both sides by 4: f = 60 ÷ 4 = $15 per flashlight.

check.stem: Why is one an equation and the other an inequality?
choices: The flashlights cost exactly $60, but the budget is a limit she must stay under
Because equations are for money and inequalities are for counting
check.explanation: 'Exactly' points to one value, so it is an equation. A budget — 'at most' — allows a whole range of values, so it is an inequality.

connect.modelAnswer: Budget: 320 + r ≤ 500, so r ≤ 180 — she can spend at most $180 more. Flashlights: 4f = 60, so f = $15 each. The budget is an inequality because any amount up to $180 is allowed; the flashlight cost is an equation because there is exactly one answer.

The 'or equal' bar means the boundary counts — that sets your circle type. Then test a bigger number to find the shading.
